summary: Iteration 8 — Safety & Wellbeing Moderation Layer frontend + recipient controls + PH resources + FAQ. Backend: 11/11 pytest cases PASS (PH resources with NCMH 1553 / Hopeline / DSWD; /moderate/appeal 200; /moderate/rewrite empty→400; GREEN sadness delivers with consent_level=recipient and visibility=private; RED threat 422 blocked; anchor-settings GET default, PUT approval+persistence, invalid who→400, unauth→401; visibility ceiling: recipient consent → shared/public both 403; report flow → visibility flips to private + reported=true). Frontend Playwright: /with/ayesha headline reads 'Leave Ayesha a little kindness.' (kindness framing, no 'reason to stay'); 8 reason chips render with correct testids; clicking reason-type-smile updates headline to 'Give Ayesha a reason to smile.'; 3 consent radio options (recipient/circle/public) with recipient default; crisis-disclaimer mentions 'not a crisis or emergency service'. YELLOW hold path: guilt/pressure text triggers moderation-hold-panel with moderation-suggestion, use-suggestion-btn, edit-original-btn, appeal-btn; clicking use-suggestion returns to form with textarea prefilled with the softened suggestion; resubmitting delivers 'Tucked in gently.'. RED block path: threat text triggers moderation-blocked-panel with write-new-btn and appeal-blocked-btn; clicking appeal-blocked-btn fires POST /api/moderate/appeal → 200 and shows the 'Review requested' toast. Landing FAQ: exactly 12 items; last (Q12) is 'How does Anchor protect me from harmful or pressuring messages?' and its answer contains 'five-level', 'review', and 'not a crisis'; Q10 'Can I control exactly what supporters see?' answer mentions 'two layers' and 'public'; Q11 Reasons/Memories/Forever answer no longer contains 'to stay'. /safety Resources tab has country-filter-philippines pill; clicking it shows NCMH, Hopeline, DSWD cards. /dashboard (authenticated via seeded session_token cookie) shows anchor-settings-card with anchor-who-anyone/approval/off, require-approval-toggle, allow-anonymous-toggle; switching to approval persists across full page reload; four-state visibility buttons per item (vis-private/shared/forever/public × 12 items each) confirming the 4-state row; wall-report-btn-{id} present. Approval E2E: setting anchor-who-approval + submitting anonymous message from a fresh browser context shows 'waiting for approval' panel to supporter; back on dashboard pending-{id} banner + approve-{id} button appear; clicking approve makes banner disappear. Mobile 390x844 on /with/ayesha, /dashboard, /safety: scrollWidth == clientWidth == 390 (no horizontal overflow). Anchor settings restored to who=anyone, require_approval=false, allow_anonymous=true at the end of testing.
critical_code_review_comments: AnchorPublic.jsx cleanly maps 422 detail {moderation, suggestion, sender_support} to the ModerationPanel (hold vs blocked). parseDetail tries JSON.parse(e.message) which relies on api client stringifying detail — works today but could regress if the api util changes; consider surfacing the raw fetch response.detail directly.

server.py POST /api/hope/{slug} correctly forces visibility='private' on insert regardless of consent_level (recipient controls sharing later). It also enforces CONSENT_ORDER ceiling in POST /hope/{item_id}/visibility (recipient<circle<public) — verified with 403 responses.

POST /api/hope/{item_id}/report is anonymous (no auth) and flips visibility to private + sets reported=true. This is the correct behavior per spec but note that any unauthenticated actor can force any item to private by knowing its ID; abuse guard here would be worth adding (rate limit reports per fingerprint).
Anchor settings PUT accepts arbitrary boolean values; the API validates 'who' enum but doesn't validate booleans strictly — Pydantic v2 will coerce. Fine for MVP.

Landing FAQS is a flat const with 12 entries; the moderation FAQ text (~140 words) accurately reflects the 5-level layer, human review, and crisis disclaimer. Q10 clearly explains the two-layer consent model. Q11 (Reasons/Memories/Forever) no longer contains the phrase 'to stay' — matches the new kindness framing.
Public /with/ayesha crisis-disclaimer footer is present and includes an anchor to /safety — good.
